title: Algebraicity and local finite presentation of the stack of flat coherent families
statement: For a scheme $S$ and a separated, flat morphism $f:X\to S$ of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $\mathcal C_f$ be the category fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes whose objects over $T\to S$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_T}$-modules $F$ of finite presentation, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$ [pqf-def-coherent, def-pc-base-change]. Here support proper over $T$ means that there are a closed immersion $i:Z\to X_T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z\to T$ proper and a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $G$ of finite type with $i_*G\cong F$. Here finite presentation of a module means locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules, and flat over $T$ means that $F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for every $x\mapsto t$. Arrows over $u:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $u_X^*F_1\cong F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\mathcal C_f$ is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Its structure morphism to $S$ is locally of finite presentation, meaning that a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal C_f$ has locally finitely presented composite $U\to S$. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08WC, theorem-coherent-algebraic (flat case), and moduli.tex Tag 0DLZ, lemma-coherent-qs-lfp. Category: quot.tex situation-coherent.

proof.text: Regard the schemes $X,S$ as their representable algebraic spaces. The identity scheme charts identify the space local finite-presentation condition with the scheme condition. For every affine scheme $V\to S$ the pullback of $h_X\to h_S$ is represented by the scheme $X\times_SV$, which is quasi-compact because quasi-compactness is stable under base change and $V$ is affine; the same applies to the diagonal, so quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are unchanged. The diagonal of $h_X\to h_S$ is the representable sheaf of the scheme diagonal, a closed immersion; every scheme base change of it is a closed immersion because closed immersions are stable under base change, so separatedness is also unchanged. Thus $f:X\to S$ satisfies the separated finite-presentation hypotheses of the general coherent-stack theorem with parameter base $B=S$ and ambient base $S$.

source.place: Situation 08KB and Tag 09DS (theorem-coherent-algebraic-general), specialized to schemes and B=S.

proof.text: For each $S$-scheme $T$, use the quasi-coherent Zariski/small-etale equivalence on $X_T$. The finiteness comparison preserves and reflects finite presentation and finite type. Relative flatness is the same condition on the identity chart; on any other etale chart it is equivalent by relative-flatness detection on flat source maps, since etale maps are flat. A closed subspace of the scheme $X_T$ is a scheme: base change its representable closed immersion by the identity of $X_T$. Conversely a scheme closed immersion defines a space closed immersion, since its scheme base changes are closed immersions by base-change stability. The closed-pushforward comparison of the equivalence identifies the proper-support presentations $i_*G\simeq F$ on the two sites (on every affine open its inverse image is the affine quotient, giving quasi-compactness; its diagonal is an isomorphism, giving separatedness). The map $h_Z\to h_T$ is representable by schemes (its scheme base changes are the scheme fibre products), so by the representable properness test it is proper as a morphism of spaces if and only if every scheme base change $Z\times_TT'\to T'$ is proper; since proper scheme morphisms are stable under base change, this holds exactly when $Z\to T$ is proper. The tensor-pullback comparison identifies the pullback-isomorphism arrows over every $T\to T_1$. Hence these equivalences identify the entire fibred groupoid $\mathcal C_f$ with $\mathcal C_{X/S}$ of the general coherent-stack theorem: the map $T\to B=S$ in its objects is the already specified structural map.

source.place: Situation 08KB; the Zariski/etale comparison uses descent.tex Tags 03DX, 03LC, 05VG, and morphisms.tex Tag 02JZ.

proof.text: Apply the existing general coherent-stack theorem to $f$ from step 1. Its algebraicity assertion gives a representable diagonal and smooth surjective scheme atlas for $\mathcal C_{X/S}$. Since $B=S$ is a scheme, its final clause also gives a locally finitely presented structural composite of that atlas to $S$. The equivalence in step 2 identifies descent data and their effective objects, so the stack condition transfers. Transport the atlas and diagonal along that equivalence. All scheme base changes of the atlas are identified by that equivalence, and its structural composite to $S$ is unchanged. This proves both algebraicity and the stated local finite presentation of $\mathcal C_f$. The cited theorem imposes neither Noetherianity nor ambient flatness, so the extra flatness assumption on $f$ causes no restriction.
